title: Cross-region DR runbook + Terraform orchestration for Private (VPC) deployments
creator: Ariana Patel
body:
Goal: Build a repeatable, safe automation pipeline that performs cross-region failover drills for Private (VPC) deployments using Terraform modules, orchestrated workflows, and health-check gating. The output should be: reusable Terraform/IaC modules for playbook steps, a CI workflow to run drills (with operator approval gates), an automated smoke test suite to validate SLOs during drill, and an incident-ready runbook with rollback steps and telemetry checks.

Scope:
- Author modular Terraform for: provisioning warm standby stacks in a secondary region, cross-region networking (VPN/BGP or Transit Gateway attachments), DNS automation for controlled traffic shifts (Route53 weighted records or external DNS), and KMS/Vault replication hooks where applicable.
- Implement health-checks that run pre-drill, mid-drill, and post-drill: node-level GPU availability, model-serving readiness, KV cache warm status, end-to-end latency p95, ingress e2e path, and storage mount validation.
- Create a CI pipeline (GitHub Actions + self-hosted runner in customer-like VPC) that runs drills on a schedule or on-demand. The pipeline must include "dry-run" Terraform plan previews, an approval step (Slack/Console), an orchestrator that performs staged traffic shifts (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and automated rollback on failure.
- Add cheap synthetic traffic generator (locally containerized faker) plus dataset-based evals to validate semantic quality regressions during drill.
- Provide a runbook page (Confluence/Drive link placeholder) and post-drill checklist: observability playbooks, alert escalation, postmortem template.

Design decisions / constraints:
- Warm-standby vs cold-standby: choose warm-standby (minimal extra cost) for customer-facing clusters where RTO target < 15 minutes. Cold warm hybrids allowed for low-priority workloads.
- DNS approach: prefer weighted DNS with short TTL controlled by automation for customers on Route53. For customers on enterprise DNS appliances, provide a manual operator step in the workflow.
- Networking modes: support Transit Gateway + TGW attachments for AWS multi-account customers and VPN/BGP for co-located on-prem customers.
- Secrets: never copy root KMS keys; prefer cross-region CMK replication or Vault replication flows. All key actions must be audited.

Acceptance criteria:
- Terraform modules checked into infra/modules/dr-runbook with unit-style tests (terraform-compliance or kitchen-terraform) and example usage in infra/examples/private-cross-region-warm.yaml.
- CI pipeline in infra/.github/workflows/drill.yml that can run a non-destructive dry-run and a destructive drill in a sandbox account after manual approval.
- Automated smoke tests (smoke/ directories) that assert model-serving readiness, latency p95 < target, and token-cost sanity checks.
- A documented operator runbook with clear abort/rollback steps and a template postmortem.
- Drill run produces telemetry: Prometheus snapshot, sample traces, and a generated report uploaded to the internal dashboard.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: cross-cloud replication orchestration (will be a follow-up), enterprise DNS adapters beyond Route53 (adapter skeleton only).
acceptance_criteria: Terraform modules for warm-standby provisioning exist and are reusable
CI pipeline supports dry-run and approved destructive drills
Health checks and smoke tests validate model-serving and SLO targets
Runbook and postmortem template are published
Telemetry artifacts produced and stored after drill
comments: 2026-02-18 Ariana Patel: Initial draft — capturing design constraints and acceptance criteria. Recommend warm-standby for most customer classes to meet RTO targets.
2026-02-25 Marcus Chen: Pulled initial terraform module skeleton into infra/modules/dr-runbook branch. Blocking: need KMS replication guidance from Security (security review required).

2026-03-02 Lina Rodriguez (SRE): Added Prometheus/Alertmanager rules and a smoke test harness (pytest) to validate p95 latency and error-rate during the shift. Noted flaky metrics on small clusters — will add retries to health probes.

2026-03-05 Marcus Chen: Implemented staged traffic shift logic in run-drill script. Added manual approval step via Slack interactive message. Next: add automated rollback thresholds and a dry-run mode for scheduled rehearsals.

2026-03-10 Priya Nair (Security): Reviewed secrets replication notes. Recommended using cross-account IAM roles and Vault OIDC replication rather than replicating KMS keys. Marked security_review_required=true.
2026-03-10 Marcus Chen: Updated ticket status to Planned and set estimate to 8 points. Assigned to self for implementation after design signoff.
